thornwick-raid.name: The Wardens at Thornwick
intro: A Warden column has come up the road from the ford: seven companies, crossbows, pikes, and riders on loftbucks. Thornwick's gate is shut and everyone who can hold a weapon is on the yard.
Click one of your companies (the blue banners), then click the ground to send it there, or click a red company to attack it. Orders take longer to reach companies far from your own.
Break them, or hold until dark and they'll pull back. Space pauses; + and - change the speed.

plan.note: The foot cross at the road ford and come at the gate; crossbows close to cover them.
Their riders swing west through the wood, across the wood ford, for the postern.
When the attack falters, the reserve goes in at the gate.
The east crossbows climb the knoll to shoot down into the yard.

stratagems.name: Riders wait in the west wood
stratagems.text: Your kith riders slip out before dawn and lie up in the wood by the wood ford. Hidden until they strike, and the first blow lands hard.

opinions.rider: "The wood's thick enough to hide a buck. Just."
opinions.commander: "Only worth it if they come that way."
opinions.skirmisher: "Let me take them. I know that wood."

stratagems.name: Stakes before the gate
stratagems.text: Sharpened stakes all across the ground in front of the gate. Anyone fighting there fights slower and bleeds for it, riders worst.

opinions.vanguard: "Leave a gap for us to go out through."
opinions.artisan: "Give me a day and the timber."

stratagems.name: Fires on the knoll
stratagems.text: Lanterns and cookfires all over the north-east knoll, as if a company held it. Their crossbows won't try for it, and the column comes on less sure of itself.

opinions.scholar: "A captain who sees fires sees what he expects."

lockside-hold.name: Corvel's hatchery
intro: Corvel's hatchery, at the head of the Lockside cut. The yard wall, the brood house behind it, the canal in front with its two lock bridges. Your first command.
A Warden column is coming up from the south: foot, pikes, crossbows, and riders. They have to cross the canal at one of the lock bridges to reach you.
Break them, or hold until dark.

plan.note: The foot go for the west lock bridge and on to the gate; the pikes take the east bridge; crossbows line the south bank.
Their riders go round through the willows, over the east bridge, for the cart gate.
When the attack falters, the reserve comes up the middle.

stratagems.name: Raise the west lock bridge
stratagems.text: The lock-keepers can wind the west bridge up out of reach. Everything they send has to come over the east bridge, under your east bows, the long way round.

opinions.artisan: "Give me the lock-keepers and it's up by dawn."
opinions.commander: "One bridge is one fight. I like one fight."
opinions.talker: "The keepers will do it for the Commons. Ask them nicely."

stratagems.name: Second company in the willows
stratagems.text: Your second company lies up in the willows by the east bridge. Hidden until they strike, and anyone who comes that way meets them first.

opinions.skirmisher: "Willows are good cover. Wet, but good."
opinions.rider: "If their riders come round, they'll come through there."

stratagems.name: Stakes before the gate
stratagems.text: Stakes across the ground in front of Corvel's gate. Whoever reaches the gate fights slowly there, and bleeds.

opinions.vanguard: "Leave a gap for us to go out through."

march-cloudline.name: The march on the terraces
intro: You've turned the Commons on the clans of the Cloudline. They knew you were coming: they're up on the terraces, behind their field walls, and they know every gate in them.
This time you're the ones attacking. Break every company they have. The walls and the high ground favour them, so go through the gates, or round.
Click a blue company, then the ground or a red company. Space pauses.

plan.note: They hold the walls. When you close, the terrace men come down through the west gate behind their slingers.
If the first wall goes, their herders ride out of the east gate at whatever is nearest.

stratagems.name: Come up in the morning fog
stratagems.text: March by night and be under their walls before the fog lifts. The first blow lands before they're sure you're there.

opinions.skirmisher: "The fog lies thick till mid-morning up there."
opinions.commander: "Fog cuts both ways. Keep the companies close."

stratagems.name: Riders round the east end
stratagems.text: Your kith riders go round through the trees at the east end and come at the terraces from the side.

opinions.rider: "Loftbucks can climb that. Ours can too."
opinions.guardian: "And if their herders are waiting there?"

march-millbridge.name: The march on Millbridge
intro: Millbridge has shut its gate on you. The town militia hold the old bridge and the wall beyond it, with the river in front.
You're attacking: break every company they have. The bridge is narrow; there's a ford further east.
Click a blue company, then the ground or a red company. Space pauses.

plan.note: They hold the bridge. Once you're across, the militia come out of the gate to push you back into the river.

stratagems.name: Cross at the east ford by night
stratagems.text: Your riders and the pikes cross at the ford before dawn and come at the bridge from its own side.

opinions.rider: "The ford's knee-deep this time of year."

stratagems.name: Shout terms across the river
stratagems.text: Tell them who you are and what you'll do after. Some of the militia knew you when you were their friend.

march-millcities.name: The march on Cinderwick
intro: The mill owners of Cinderwick have hired every guard they could and armed their foremen. They hold the canal and the foundry yards behind it.
You're attacking: break every company they have. Two swing bridges cross the cut; the yard wall has three gates.
Click a blue company, then the ground or a red company. Space pauses.

plan.note: They hold the bridges. When you're over, the foremen's pikes come out of the middle gate.
When it goes badly for them, their riders and the reserve come out of the side gates.

stratagems.name: The mill hands open a gate
stratagems.text: Someone inside owes the Commons. Your second company slips into the yards before dawn and waits behind the wall.

opinions.guardian: "If it's a trap, that company's gone."

stratagems.name: Swing the east bridge shut
stratagems.text: A lock-keeper swings the east bridge out of line in the night. They can't come over it at you; you take only the west.

tarsis-yield.name: The flat below Tarsis
intro: Vela Orme's companies on the flat below the fort, with blunted spears and the sun behind them. Your companies facing them.
No killing. First side to yield the field. Every sellsword in Tarsis is on the wall to watch.
Vela fights the way she's paid to: she'll test your flanks, then come with her riders where you're thin.

plan.note: Vela's foot cross the dry bed together; her bows take the east rise.
When your line is fixed, her riders come round the west rise for your flank.

stratagems.name: Hold the west rise
stratagems.text: Put a company on the low rise to the west before Vela's riders think of it. Riders don't like going uphill into spears.

opinions.commander: "She'll come round the west. Riders always come round the side with the most grass."
opinions.rider: "The rise is soft on the near side. They'll slow."

stratagems.name: Wait for the sun
stratagems.text: Ask for the yield at noon, not morning, so the sun isn't in our faces.

opinions.scholar: "She picked the hour. Make her pick another."

ashby-mole.name: Ashby's harbour mouth
intro: The Commons' boats are chained across Port Ashby's harbour mouth, and the harbour council wants them gone.
Ashby's marines are coming out along the mole and wading the shallows at both ends. Rue leads them.
Hold the harbour mouth until the tide turns, or break them.

plan.note: The marines come up the mole; two more companies wade the shallows at either end; crossbows line the quay.
When it falters, the Guild's own marines come up the mole behind them.

stratagems.name: A fire boat down the mole
stratagems.text: An old lighter full of tar, lit and pushed along the mole's side. Whoever is on the mole when it goes up will not stay there.

opinions.artisan: "Tar, a candle, and a long pole. I've done worse for a wedding."
opinions.guardian: "Fire on water goes where the wind says. Mind the wind."

stratagems.name: Wait for the tide
stratagems.text: Fight at high water: the shallows are too deep to wade, and everything they send has to come up the mole.

opinions.scholar: "Ashby's tide table is on every tavern wall."

spindle-gate.name: The Spindle gate
intro: Vantry's outer ward. The Spindle wall stands across the street, with its gate and a postern. Behind it, the ward runs up to the Broodhouse.
You're attacking: break every company they have. The gate is strong; the postern is narrow, and nobody's watching it closely.
Click a blue company, then the ground or a red company. Space pauses.

plan.note: They hold the gate. Once you're through it, the Wardens in the ward close in from both sides.
When it goes badly, their riders and the Broodhouse guard come down the road.

stratagems.name: Ladders on the wall
stratagems.text: Light scaling ladders, carried up in the dark. Your pikes and bows go over the wall either side of the gate while it's still shut.

opinions.artisan: "Light enough for a child to carry. That was the point."
opinions.guardian: "Ladders are slow. Slow is dead, under crossbows."

stratagems.name: The postern, before dawn
stratagems.text: A company goes through the postern in the last of the dark, and comes at the gate guard from behind.

opinions.skirmisher: "Nobody watches a postern. Nobody ever has."
opinions.commander: "And if it's watched, that company's alone."

stratagems.name: The runaways open the drains
stratagems.text: Posy's runaways have been in the ward for a week. At the first push they set the Wardens' stores alight and shout that the Commons is in the drains.

opinions.talker: "Children are the best spies in Vantry. Nobody looks at them."
opinions.hero: "Not one of them goes near a fight."

spindle-gate.lost: Thrown back from the Spindle gate
